newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end lower on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end lower on political uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower in thin trading on Tuesday as investors remained sidelined by a deepening crisis between Israel and the Palestinians, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.69 percent, or 4.33 points, to 251.70 on low all-share turnover of 99 million shekels against 89 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.59 percent lower at 258.20.
"Trading is still very sluggish but I believe that this is only a correction before the market can regain the positive momentum," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.

"The main reason for today's decline was the political uncertainty. The market was also affected by expectations for a relatively high February CPI (consumer price index)," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
The trader said the correction might continue for several days but the overall outlook for the market was still positive.

Senior Palestinian negotiator and Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo said on Monday peace talks with Israel were passing through a serious crisis over an Israeli redeployment plan in the West Bank rejected by the PLO.
Analysts predict the February inflation figure to be released on Friday will show a 1.2 percent rise over January.
"The earning reports published so far were positive and if it was not for the political uncertainty I believe that the market would have closed higher today," Weisberg said.
Elron Electronic Industries fell 0.75 percent to 4,526 agorot. Elron said on Tuesday that 1996 net profit rose to $11.3 million from $10.3 million in 1995.
Makhteshim Chemical Works dropped 2.5 percent to 1,801. The company reported on Tuesday that net profit last year rose to 99 million shekels from 80.5 million shekels in 1995.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which fell 1.25 percent to 399 agorot on volume of 5.8 million shekels; Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 31,198 agorot on turnover of 4.7 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 1.5 percent to 849 on volume of 4.1 million shekels.
